title: The Vine Palindrome
statement:
Ancient vine markings snake along the jungle trail. A marking is 'true' only if the sequence of letters and digits reads the same forwards and backwards once you ignore spaces, punctuation, and letter case. Given a string `s`, return True if it is such a palindrome.

Constraints:
- 0 <= len(s) <= 2 * 10^5
- s consists of printable ASCII characters

examples.input: s = "A man, a plan, a canal: Panama"

args: A man, a plan, a canal: Panama
Was it a car or a cat I saw?

hint: Point one index at each end and walk inward, skipping any character that isn't a letter or digit; stop the moment two compared letters don't match.

title: The Fossil Pair
statement:
A row of fossil weights `nums` is already sorted in ascending order. Find the two (0-indexed) fossils whose weights sum to exactly `target`, and return their indices `[i, j]` with `i < j`. Exactly one such pair exists. Because the row is already sorted, solve it with two pointers in O(1) extra space instead of a hash map.

Constraints:
- 2 <= len(nums) <= 3 * 10^4
- nums is sorted in non-decreasing order
- Exactly one valid pair exists
hint: Start one pointer at each end. If the sum is too big, pull the right pointer in; if too small, push the left pointer out — sorted order guarantees this converges.

title: Rune Reversal
statement:
A weathered tablet holds a list of runic characters `chars`. Reverse their order using O(1) extra space (swap from both ends inward) and return the reversed list.

Constraints:
- 0 <= len(chars) <= 10^5
hint: Swap the characters at the left and right pointers, then step them toward each other until they meet or cross.

title: Trail Compression
statement:
A sorted trail log `nums` records footprint markers in ascending order, but the same marker was sometimes logged multiple times in a row. Return a new list with consecutive duplicates collapsed, preserving order.

Constraints:
- 0 <= len(nums) <= 3 * 10^4
- nums is sorted in non-decreasing order
hint: Keep a 'write' pointer for the last unique value kept so far; only copy a value forward when it differs from that one.

title: Herding the Stragglers
statement:
A row of herd positions `nums` uses 0 to mark an empty slot where a straggler wandered off, and any nonzero value for a present dinosaur. Rearrange the row so every straggler slot moves to the end, while the dinosaurs keep their original relative order. Return the rearranged list.

Constraints:
- 1 <= len(nums) <= 10^4
hint: One pointer scans for nonzero values; a second pointer marks where the next kept value should land. Fill the leftover slots with zeros at the end.

title: Following the Trail
statement:
A lone raptor's path `s` may or may not be hidden within the herd's full trail `t`, formed by deleting some of the herd's steps without reordering the rest. Return True if `s` is a subsequence of `t`.

Constraints:
- 0 <= len(s) <= 100
- 0 <= len(t) <= 10^4
hint: Walk both strings with one pointer each. Advance the t-pointer every step, but only advance the s-pointer when the characters match.

title: Merging the Herds
statement:
Two herds' ages, `a` and `b`, are each already sorted ascending. Merge them into one combined sorted list.

Constraints:
- 0 <= len(a), len(b) <= 5000
hint: Walk a pointer through each sorted herd, always appending whichever current age is smaller, then append whatever remains of the other herd.

title: Sorting the Egg Clutch
statement:
A nest holds eggs represented as 0 (red), 1 (green), or 2 (blue) in scrambled order. Rearrange them in place so all reds come first, then greens, then blues — in a single pass using three pointers (low / mid / high), without a full sort. Return the sorted list.

Constraints:
- 1 <= len(eggs) <= 300
- eggs[i] is 0, 1, or 2
hint: The Dutch national flag technique: 'low' marks the boundary before reds, 'high' marks the boundary after blues, and 'mid' scans between them, swapping and moving boundaries as it goes.

title: The Widest Watering Hole
statement:
A row of jungle trees has heights `heights[i]`. Any two trees, together with the ground between them, can form a watering hole holding a volume of `min(height of the two trees) * (distance between them)`. Find the maximum volume any two trees can hold.

Constraints:
- 2 <= len(heights) <= 10^5
- 0 <= heights[i] <= 10^4
hint: Start pointers at both ends. The volume is capped by the shorter tree, so moving the taller tree's pointer inward can never help — always move the shorter side.

title: The Zero-Sum Excavation
statement:
BOSS TRIAL — Deep in the dig site, three fossil weights (which may be negative) must be found that sum to exactly zero. Given a list `nums`, return every unique triplet of values `[a, b, c]` with `a + b + c == 0`. No duplicate triplets, and each triplet's three values must be listed in non-decreasing order.

Constraints:
- 3 <= len(nums) <= 3000
- -10^5 <= nums[i] <= 10^5
hint: Sort the array first. Fix one value, then two-pointer the rest of the array inward looking for the complement sum — skip over repeated values to avoid duplicate triplets.
